text: There stood, facing the open window, a comfortable, roomy armchair, into which she sank with a physical exhaustion that seemed to reach into her soul. <break time="0.8s" /> Through the window she could see, in the open square before her house, trees whose tops were trembling with the new spring life. <break time="0.8s" /> The delicious breath of rain was in the air, and in the street below a peddler was crying his wares to passers by. <break time="0.8s" /> Faintly she could hear someone singing a distant song, and countless sparrows were twittering in the eaves of the houses. <break time="0.8s" /> In the west facing her window, the clouds had piled one above another, but patches of blue sky were showing here and there through them. <break time="0.8s" /> She sat with her head thrown back upon the cushion of the chair, quite motionless, except when a sob came up into her throat. <break time="0.8s" /> She was like a child who has cried itself to sleep and still sobs in its dreams, long after the crying has stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> She was young, with a fair, calm face, whose lines showed a long habit of holding back her feelings and also a certain strength. <break time="0.8s" /> But now there was a dull stare in her eyes, which were fixed far away on one of those patches of blue sky.
